paramsNote: Engine parameters supplied by the coordinator. They do NOT necessarily equal the printed plan dimensions below - see overview for the values actually printed on the plan sheets.

widthAtBase.note: Base layout outside-to-outside (p11). Only the non-beveled method is drawn for this model.

baseSideLength.note: Common base section bottom plate, long point to long point. The base layout sheet itself does not dimension the bay; 8'-11 11/16" / sin(18 deg) = 29'- 3/8" confirms the decagon.

overview.doorOpeningNote: No finished rough opening is published. Basic doorway: double 2x6 / 38x140 header at 6'-3" / 1905 mm, opening framed 8'- 1/8" / 2442 mm wide overall with the head at 9'-5 13/16" / 2892 mm. Fancy doorway: double 2x6 / 38x140 header at 6'-11 11/16" / 2126 mm plus (2) trimmer studs at 6'-8" / 2032 mm.
overview.buildMethod: Non-beveled method only. The Model Specific Notes sheet (p3) says: minimum 2x4 / 38x89 lumber, and 'This zome should be constructed in the non beveled method, as the framed [sic] are too deep to run through the table saw.' The bevel-angle column is still printed but is not used for this build method.
overview.doorwayVariants: This model ships TWO complete doorway designs - 'Basic' (a shed-roofed awning over a wide opening, 2 special base sections) and 'Fancy' (a gable dormer like the 25' zome). Each has its own exploded view, component list, entry deck and cut sheets, and they give DIFFERENT strut and panel counts. Pick one before taking off materials.
overview.geometryNote: Zome, 10-sided plan, 5 concentric bands of rhombic panels labelled z1 (top/centre) through z5 (widest), plus special half panels that differ between the Basic and Fancy doorway variants. All struts are the same length; only the corner (miter) angles and the dihedral-derived bevel angles change band to band.

length.note: Overall panel length - identical for every regular panel edge and for the sloped edges of every special panel.

crossSection.note: The Model Specific Notes sheet calls for a minimum of 2x4 / 38x89 lumber. The materials list buys (115) 2x4x12 / 38x89x3.6m for the frame panels. Deeper members may be substituted if the plan is scaled.

strut.bevelNote: Bevel is not a single value. Each panel band has a top bevel (the two struts pointing toward the centre/top) and a bottom bevel (the two struts pointing outward/down). Where two bands meet the bevels match. Not used in the non-beveled method, which is the method specified for this model. See panels[].bevels.
strut.miterNote: All miter angles in the plans are stated as OFF 90 degrees - i.e. the number is what you set the miter saw to. Within one regular panel every strut shares the same miter angle.

midLength.note: Width across the panel at mid height, outside framing; use for jig layout.

geometryChecks.method: For a rhombus of side s with printed mid-width (short diagonal) d, the spanned corner angle is 2*asin((d/2)/s); the saw miter (off 90 deg) must equal |90 - that angle| or |90 - (180 - that angle)|. Computed from the imperial figures with s = 66.375 in (5'-6 3/8").

specialPanels.check: Miters 4.7 / 42.7 / 42.7 give interior angles 85.3 / 47.3 / 47.3 (sum 179.9). With base 7'-6" / 2286 mm the equal sides compute to 5'-6 3/8" / 1686 mm - matches the printed value.
Miters 37.2 / 15.6 / 37.2 give interior angles 52.8 / 74.4 / 52.8 (sum 180). With sides 5'-6 3/8" the vertical edge computes to 80.29 in = 6'-8 5/16"; printed 6'-8 1/4" / 2038 mm. Within 1/16 in.

Miters 15.6 / 52.8 / 52.8 give interior angles 105.6 / 37.2 / 37.2 (sum 180). With base 8'-9 13/16" / 2688 mm the equal sides compute to 66.41 in = 5'-6 3/8" / 1686 mm - matches. (This is the sheet the 25' plan mis-copied from.)
Legs 3'-4 1/8" and 4'-4 7/8" give a hypotenuse of 66.38 in = 5'-6 3/8" and corner angles 52.8 / 37.2, matching the printed 37.2 / 0 / 52.8 miters.
Miters 33.1 / 23.8 / 33.1 give interior angles 56.9 / 66.2 / 56.9 (sum 180). Third side computes to 72.47 in = 6'-0 1/2" / 1841 mm - matches the printed value.

geometryChecks.metricCrossCheck: Every metric mid-length and side length re-checks to within 1 mm of the imperial value, and the metric miter computation reproduces the same results.
geometryChecks.conclusion: All five rhombus bands and all five special panels are internally consistent. No dimensional errors were found in the panel geometry of this model.

pdfIssues.issue: The eighth deck member is printed as '586' mm. The imperial sheet gives 2'-3" for the same member, which is 686 mm, and the imperial series steps down by a constant 15 9/16" (2270, 1875, 1478, 1083, 686, 291 mm). 586 breaks that pattern by exactly 100 mm and is almost certainly a digit typo.
pdfIssues.severity: moderate - 10 pieces would be cut 100 mm short

pdfIssues.sheet: Doorway: Fancy, Wall Panel D (p26), imperial vs metric
pdfIssues.issue: The three wall-sheathing dimensions do not convert between editions: top edge 5'-5 1/4" (1657 mm) vs 1667 mm; short side 6'-6 3/8" (1991 mm) vs 2016 mm; tall side 9'-5 13/16" (2891 mm) vs 2926 mm. The bottom edge (4'-7" / 1397 mm) does agree. Note the metric top edge (1667) equals the panel's sloped top PLATE length, so the metric sheathing dimension may simply have been copied from the cut list.

The z4 half vert upper-edge bevel is printed as '11'. Everywhere else in the plan set the z4 top bevel is 11.1 (and the panel's lower edge correctly carries the z4 bottom bevel of 15.4). Almost certainly a truncated 11.1.

pdfIssues.sheet: Doorway: Fancy, Wall Panel D (p26), IMPERIAL edition
pdfIssues.issue: A stud is printed '7-9 7/8"' with no foot mark. The metric 2384 mm confirms it means 7'-9 7/8".
The dimension label reads 'Outside to Ouside' (missing t).
Reads 'as the framed are too deep to run through the table saw' - should be 'frames'.

Imperial call-outs survive on the metric edition: Entry Deck Basic (p15) still says '16 O.C.'; the Deck note (p12) reads 'Blocking Joists are 610mm on' with 'center' truncated; the Sheet Layout leader on p29 still labels the panels '(24) 76x150"'; and the Wall Panel D plate reads '1667 Short 33 deg', dropping the 'L to' prefix used on the imperial sheet.

The exploded 'Sheathing / Siding' piece is dimensioned 4'-5 13/16" / 1367 mm long by 4 1/2" / 115 mm high, which is the SPECIAL (half) base section length. The sheathing length for the eight common base sections is never dimensioned - use the common bottom plate length (8'-11 11/16" / 2735 mm).

pdfIssues.sheet: Exploded Views (p5 and p6) and Tools & Materials (p4)
pdfIssues.issue: Two complete and mutually exclusive component lists are published (Basic doorway: 223 struts / 46 reg / 13 special / 8+2 base sections; Fancy doorway: 206 struts / 44 reg / 10 special / 8 base sections), while the materials page lists both doors together. A take-off must choose one doorway; adding both over-buys.
No finished door rough-opening size is published for either doorway variant; only header, trimmer and framed-opening dimensions are given.
The strut length (5'-6 3/8" / 1686 mm) is printed in a bare box with no 'Overall Length for all panels' caption, unlike the 20' and 25' sheets which label it.

This model's strut length (5'-6 3/8" / 1686 mm) is the value that was mistakenly copied onto the 25' / 7.5m plan's 'z4 half (base)' special-panel sheet, where the correct side length is 4' 8" / 1423 mm. Recorded here so the two files stay cross-referenced.
